title: No package metadata or license on any crate; unit files point Documentation= at an unrelated third party
description:
None of the six member manifests declare license, description, repository, readme, keywords or categories, there is no LICENSE file at the repo root, and no crate sets 'publish = false'. The repo has no git remote.

Most of that is fine for a private project and I am not filing it as a defect. Two parts are worth acting on:

1. No license file at all. README.md, DESIGN.md, SPEC-HIA.md and PRFAQ.md read as material intended to be shared. Unlicensed source is all-rights-reserved by default, which is probably not the intent, and it is the one thing that is awkward to fix retroactively once other people have contributed. (Licensing choice is the maintainer's call — this is a note that the choice has not been recorded, not a recommendation of a particular license.)

2. Concretely wrong, not just missing: systemd/personad.service and systemd/personad.socket both set
       Documentation=https://github.com/persona-id/persona
   github.com/persona-id is Persona Identities Inc., an unrelated company. Anyone running 'systemctl --user help personad' or reading the installed unit is sent to a third party's repository for support on this daemon. Point it at the real repo or drop the line.

Adding 'publish = false' to the five non-library crates costs one line each and removes the accidental-publish question entirely.
close_reason:
Split outcome: the licensing half is already done, and the packaging half is decided and implemented in e0cb678.

ALREADY DONE, so stale in the bead: 'No license file at all' and 'no crate declares license'. All six crates declare license = "Apache-2.0", and the repo root carries LICENSE and LICENSE-CC-BY-4.0. The Documentation= URL pointing at github.com/persona-id (Persona Identities Inc., an unrelated company) was corrected in 930072e -- systemd/personad.service now points at github.com/MarkAtwood/project-persona, and it is the only Documentation= line left in the tree. No licensing choice was made or touched here; per Mark's standing rule that is his call alone.

DECIDED AND DONE: publish = false on all six crates, which was the bead's own concrete recommendation ('costs one line each and removes the accidental-publish question entirely'). Verified by cargo rather than by reading the file back: 'cargo publish --dry-run -p persona-core' now exits with 'cannot be published'.

NOT DONE, deliberately: description, repository, keywords and categories. Those exist to serve a crates.io listing and a docs.rs page, neither of which an unpublishable crate has. Adding them now would be metadata nobody reads, kept in sync by nobody. They belong with whichever crate first becomes publishable.

Fact worth keeping for that day: the name 'persona' is already registered on crates.io (2019-10-24, 'Reserving this crate for a Mozilla inside-joke'), so the CLI binary crate cannot publish under its current name. persona-core, persona-grpc, persona-attestors and personad all appeared unregistered as of 2026-09-15.
